raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation Profiling a 1 M-token prefill of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4× B200 (TP4 + EP4, DSPARK, the cookbook low-latency recipe) shows two kinds of work that a *group* of layers shares but that the code redoes *per layer*, and both are O(context²) over a chunked prefill. **1. Every ratio-2 index-source layer scans the whole context.** `candidate_source_layer_id` is a single layer id in the checkpoint, and `uses_candidates` is one global `layer_id` comparison, so only the ratio-1 index group gets the publish/consume treatment. On DSv4.1-Flash — `index_source_layer_ids = [2, 8, 14, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36]`, `candidate_source_layer_id = 20`, `compress_ratios = [0,0] + [2]*18 + [1]*20 + [0,0,0]` — that leaves layers 2, 8 and 14 each running a full dense `sm100_mqa_logits` scan over the entire compressed context, every prefill chunk. In the 1 M trace the dense indexer family is **7.19 s of a 26 s prefill (27.7 %)** and grows **+3.0 ms per 16 K of context per chunk**, which is exactly `Σ 1/ratio = 3×½ + 1×1 = 2.5` context-widths per chunk. **2. The compressed-cache dequant runs once per consumer layer, not once per kv_source group.** Compressed KV for ratios 1/2 is owned by a kv_source layer (`kv_source_layer_ids = [2, 8, 14, 20]`) and read by every later layer of that ratio, but `_forward_prefill_sparse` dequantizes the whole group cache into the bf16 workspace on each of them. At 256 K that is **124.6 ms per prefill** growing **+0.77 ms per 16 K**. The HIP backend already memoizes exactly this (`_OpusPrefillState.compressed_kv`); the CUDA path did not. The dequant kernel itself was also shaped one token per program, issuing 64-element loads at ~1.1 TB/s effective. Related issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/42170 ## Modifications **1. Per-ratio candidate publishing** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_PER_RATIO_CANDIDATES`, default **off**). The first index-source layer of each compress-ratio group publishes candidate blocks and the later index sources of that group consume them, exactly like the shipped ratio-1 publish/consume path; `candidate_metadata` becomes a per-ratio dict (one publisher today, two with the flag). Within a ratio group the index pools share one slot space and `consume_prefill` already scores the *consumer layer's own* keys through `get_index_k_cache(layer_id=...)`, so the published block schedule carries over unchanged — only which columns get scored changes. **2. Dequant dedup across a kv_source group** (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_SPARSE_PREFILL_DEQUANT_DEDUP`, default **on**). One dequant per `(workspace buffer, source cache, gather, rows, layout)` memoized on the per-chunk `SparsePrefillChunkCache`. Any key change — a different source group, a workspace reallocation, a different gather — falls back to a fresh dequant, and the c0 path invalidates the memo because its SWA gather starts at workspace offset 0 and overwrites the compressed region. This is invariant-preserving: it skips a byte-identical recomputation. **3. Vectorize the V4 paged dequant kernel** to 4 tokens per program: one `[4, 8, 64]` fp8 load (the 8-padded scale row with the pad tile masked), one `[4, 8]` scale load and one `[4, 64]` bf16 rope load per program. The dequant is elementwise, so the grid shape changes no output bit. ## Accuracy GSM8K, 200 examples, `--temperature 0`, run against both servers in the same session: | | score | score:std | |---|---|---| | baseline | 0.995 | 0.0705 | | this PR (both flags on) | 0.995 | 0.0705 | Changes 2 and 3 are bitwise-neutral by construction, and change 3 is covered by the shipped zero-tolerance self-test (`test/manual/kernels/attention/check_dsv4_dequant_k_cache.py`, `assert_close(atol=0, rtol=0)` against the torch reference), which passes on B200. ## Benchmarks Warm TTFT, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4× B200, TP4 + EP4, `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64`, bs = 1, random-token prompts, 3–4 seeds per cell: | context | baseline | + changes 2&3 | + change 1 (all) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 M (in-len 1 048 000) | 27.58 – 27.73 s | 26.52 – 26.54 s | **23.72 – 23.79 s (−14 %)** | | 256 K | 4.87 – 4.92 s | 4.82 – 4.90 s | — | Per-family kernel time from the TP-0 torch traces of the same 1 M request (64 chunks of 16 K): | family | baseline | this PR | |---|---|---| | indexer dense logits | 7 192 ms (27.7 %) | **4 883 ms (20.9 %)** | | …its growth per 16 K of context | +3.0 ms | **+1.9 ms** (`Σ 1/ratio` 2.5 → 1.5) | | …dense launches / time in the last chunk | 79 launches, 187.3 ms | **47 launches, 113.7 ms** | | …paged-sparse launches / time in the last chunk | 4 launches, 5.5 ms | 6 launches, 8.4 ms | | top-k kernels | 2 007 ms | **1 415 ms** | | GPU busy, whole prefill | 25.93 s | **23.36 s** | The two extra paged-sparse launches are layers 8 and 14 moving onto the published candidates; they cost 2.9 ms and remove 73.6 ms of dense scanning in that chunk. Dequant, 256 K prefill (TP-0 trace) and the kernel alone (idle B200, page size 256, V4 layout): | | baseline | this PR | |---|---|---| | `_dequantize_k_cache_paged` per prefill | 124.6 ms | **26.6 ms** | | …in the last chunk | 13.58 ms | **2.15 ms** | | …growth per 16 K of context | +0.77 ms | **+0.07 ms** | | kernel, 262 K rows | 0.381 ms (1.1 TB/s) | **0.089 ms (4.8 TB/s)** | | kernel, 524 K rows | 0.754 ms | **0.171 ms** | | kernel, 16 K rows | 0.019 ms | 0.020 ms (launch-bound) | A short-context side effect worth noting: the GSM8K run itself went from 34.3 s to 28.8 s (871 → 1017 output tok/s), because the ratio-2 layers also take the consume path at decode. ## Reproduction ```bash # server (add SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_PER_RATIO_CANDIDATES=1 for change 1) python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --trust-remote-code \ --tp 4 --ep-size 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 --port 31000 # kernel self-test (zero tolerance vs the torch reference) python3 test/manual/kernels/attention/check_dsv4_dequant_k_cache.py # accuracy python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-threads 32 --temperature 0 --port 31000 ``` ## Limitations and risks - Change 1 is **off by default**. It changes what the ratio-2 index sources score: 2048 candidate blocks × 8 = 16 384 positions, i.e. 12.5 % of the ratio-2 window at 256 K and 3.1 % at 1 M. The ratio-1 group already ships with the same absolute budget (1.6 % of the window at 1 M), and GSM8K is unchanged, but a longer-horizon eval on a retrieval-heavy workload would strengthen the case before flipping the default. - Change 1 is not validated under prefill context parallelism: the CP path forces `DenseBlocksBackend` for publishes, so the flag should stay off there until that fallback is lifted. - The dequant memo assumes the group's compressed cache is not rewritten between the first consumer's read and the last one's within a forward. That holds today because only the kv_source layer writes it and it does so before its own attention; the memo key still re-validates the cache pointer, the gather and the layout on every call. - All numbers are from one model and one shape family (DSv4.1-Flash, bs = 1, random-token prompts, 16 K chunks). The high-throughput cell (`--max-running-requests 256`, no spec decoding) was not measured in this round. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code: `pre-commit run --all-files` (not run locally; CI lint will confirm) - [x] Add unit tests: change 3 is covered by the existing zero-tolerance dequant self-test; changes 1 and 2 are exercised end to end by the DSv4.1-Flash B200 e2e tests, with GSM8K reported above - [x] Update documentation as needed: the new env vars are documented at their definitions in `environ.py` --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #37603101372](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37603101372) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #37739435326](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37739435326) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #37603101111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37603101111)

nodes.body:
Could we add a paired quality comparison with per-ratio candidates enabled/disabled on the same commit and prompts, including a long-context retrieval workload?

The test comment reports GSM8K scores of 0.865/0.880 with the flag on versus 0.905 with it off, while the threshold is 0.85. These samples do not establish a regression, but the current threshold also does not enforce the stated quality parity. The newly added Base-C test was skipped in the current Base run, so we still need execution evidence for that path.

+"""B200 CI: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash FP4 with per-ratio candidate publishing.
+
+With SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_PER_RATIO_CANDIDATES=1 the ratio-2 index sources consume
+the candidate blocks published by their group's first index source instead of
+running a full dense scan each. The gate: output quality (GSM8K), decode
+correctness, and the DSPARK accept length must hold at parity with the default
+path while the flag is on.
+
+Registry: base-c-test-4-gpu-b200 (per-commit, 4x B200)
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.kits.basic_decode_correctness_kit import BasicDecodeCorrectnessMixin
+from sglang.test.kits.eval_accuracy_kit import GSM8KMixin
+from sglang.test.kits.spec_decoding_kit import SpecDecodingMixin
+from sglang.test.test_utils import (
+    DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST,
+    CustomTestCase,
+    popen_launch_server,
+    terminate_and_kill_process_tree,
+    try_cached_model,
+)
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=1200, stage="base-c", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+MODEL = "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash"
+SERVER_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT = 3600
+
+_PER_RATIO_ENV = {
+    "SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_PER_RATIO_CANDIDATES": "1",
+}
+
+
+class TestDSV41FlashFP4PerRatioCandidatesB200(
+    SpecDecodingMixin,
+    BasicDecodeCorrectnessMixin,
+    GSM8KMixin,
+    CustomTestCase,
+):
+    """Cookbook low-latency recipe (TP4+EP4, DSPARK) + per-ratio candidates."""
+
+    # Measured on 4x B200 with this recipe, 200 questions: 0.865 / 0.880 with
+    # the flag on and 0.905 with it off -- all within one standard error of each
+    # other (binary score, SE ~ 0.023 at n=200), and consistent with the 0.911
+    # the MI35x V4.1 eval measures over all 1319 questions. The 0.93 the
+    # V4-Flash-0731 suites use is a different model's number. Threshold sits
+    # ~0.015 under the lowest sample, matching how the MI35x test is calibrated.
+    gsm8k_accuracy_thres = 0.85
+    # DSPARK block size 5 accepts 3.36-3.40 here, flag on or off.
+    accept_length_thres = 3.0
+    bs_1_speed_thres = 150
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.model = try_cached_model(MODEL)
+        cls.base_url = DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST
+        cls.process = popen_launch_server(
+            cls.model,
+            cls.base_url,
+            timeout=SERVER_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT,
+            other_args=[
+                "--trust-remote-code",
+                "--tp",
+                "4",
+                "--ep-size",
+                "4",
+                "--mem-fraction-static",
+                "0.8",
+                "--speculative-algorithm",
+                "DSPARK",
+                "--speculative-dspark-block-size",
+                "5",
+                "--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode",
+                "64",
+                "--disable-flashinfer-autotune",
+            ],
+            env=_PER_RATIO_ENV,
+        )
+
+    @classmethod
+    def tearDownClass(cls):
+        if hasattr(cls, "process") and cls.process:
+            terminate_and_kill_process_tree(cls.process)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main(verbosity=3)

+"""The V4 paged K-cache dequant against the torch reference, bitwise.
+
+The kernel gathers arbitrary token slots from the paged fp8+ue8m0 cache into a
+bf16 workspace; the sparse-prefill dequant dedup reuses its output across a
+kv_source group, so any deviation from the reference (masking at the
+tokens-per-program tail, slot-to-page math, int64 offsets, workspace-slice
+strides) must fail loudly and exactly."""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.dequant_k_cache import (
+    NOPE_ROPE_BYTES,
+    PADDED_SCALE_PER_TOKEN,
+    dequantize_k_cache_paged,
+    dequantize_k_cache_paged_ref,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+# (num_tokens, page_size): tails of 0/1/3 modulo the kernel's 4 tokens per
+# program, both cache page sizes the pool uses, and a many-page gather.
+CASES = [
+    (1, 64),
+    (3, 64),
+    (333, 64),
+    (256, 256),
+    (4097, 256),
+]
+
+
+def _make_cache(num_pages: int, page_size: int, device) -> torch.Tensor:
+    raw = page_size * (NOPE_ROPE_BYTES + PADDED_SCALE_PER_TOKEN)
+    bytes_per_page = (raw + NOPE_ROPE_BYTES - 1) // NOPE_ROPE_BYTES * NOPE_ROPE_BYTES
+    return torch.randint(
+        0, 256, (num_pages, bytes_per_page), dtype=torch.uint8, device=device
+    )
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.cuda.get_device_capability() >= (8, 9),
+    "needs a CUDA device with fp8 support",
+)
+class TestDSV4DequantKCachePaged(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        self.device = "cuda"
+
+    def _check(self, num_tokens, page_size, *, table_dtype=torch.int32, out=None):
+        num_pages = max(2, (num_tokens + page_size - 1) // page_size + 1)
+        cache = _make_cache(num_pages, page_size, self.device)
+        table = torch.randint(
+            0,
+            num_pages * page_size,
+            (num_tokens,),
+            dtype=table_dtype,
+            device=self.device,
+        )
+        got = dequantize_k_cache_paged(cache, table, page_size, out=out)
+        want = dequantize_k_cache_paged_ref(cache, table, page_size)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(got, want, atol=0, rtol=0, equal_nan=True)
+        if out is not None:
+            self.assertEqual(got.data_ptr(), out.data_ptr())
+
+    def test_matches_reference(self):
+        for num_tokens, page_size in CASES:
+            with self.subTest(num_tokens=num_tokens, page_size=page_size):
+                self._check(num_tokens, page_size)
+
+    def test_int64_page_table(self):
+        self._check(333, 256, table_dtype=torch.int64)
+
+    def test_workspace_slice_output(self):
+        # The sparse-prefill path hands the kernel a slice of a larger shared
+        # workspace; the kernel must honor out.stride(0) instead of assuming a
+        # freshly allocated destination.
+        num_tokens, page_size = 777, 256
+        workspace = torch.full(
+            (num_tokens + 512, 1, 512),
+            float("nan"),
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            device="cuda",
+        )
+        self._check(num_tokens, page_size, out=workspace[:num_tokens])
+        # Rows past the slice stay untouched.
+        self.assertTrue(torch.isnan(workspace[num_tokens:].float()).all())
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main(verbosity=3)

issue_comments.body:
Could we add a paired quality comparison with per-ratio candidates enabled/disabled on the same commit and prompts, including a long-context retrieval workload?

The test comment reports GSM8K scores of 0.865/0.880 with the flag on versus 0.905 with it off, while the threshold is 0.85. These samples do not establish a regression, but the current threshold also does not enforce the stated quality parity. The newly added Base-C test was skipped in the current Base run, so we still need execution evidence for that path.
